subject: Purchase routing & conditional no-PO approval request — FluxOps integration
messages:
From: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@fluxops.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration trial — onboarding & purchase order question

Hi Rafael + Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FluxOps is excited to run a short pilot integrating your embeddings API for our vector search layer. Legal asked us to check procurement rules: our onboarding form is attached but our finance team prefers invoice-based billing (no PO) for pilot contracts under $10k.

Can Redwood support an invoice-only billing path for a 3-month trial? If Redwood requires a PO, can we arrange a one-off exception with controls (prepaid credit or early invoice and 14-day payment term)? We can provide W9 and the standard vendor form (attached).

Attachments: FluxOps_Vendor_Form.pdf, FluxOps_W9.pdf, integration_scope_v1.docx

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood to confirm whether a temporary no-PO onboarding is possible for pilots and what approvals are required
- If exception needed: propose a mutual action plan and expiration date for the waiver

Looking forward,
Aisha Kumar
Head of Partnerships
FluxOps

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@fluxops.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration trial — onboarding & purchase order question

Aisha — thanks for the attachments and clear ask. Short answer: we can do a timeboxed invoice-only path for low-dollar pilot engagements, but it requires a written procurement exception and a short approval loop on our side.

Proposed exception guardrails:
- Pilot maximum: $10,000 total invoiced over 3 months
- Exception duration: 90 days (auto-expire unless converted to standard PO contract)
- Payment: Net 14, or prepaid credit hold if billing team requests
- Evidence: completed vendor form + W9 + SSO contact for security (we have integration_scope_v1 on file)

Action items I can take this to Procurement for a quick sign-off today if Marissa and Karthik are OK with the above. If Procurement needs extra controls (e.g., limited scope L2 signoff), we can add them.

Can you confirm the estimated spend and start date?

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Integration trial — procurement exception request (FluxOps)

Forwarding for procurement review — Rafael proposes a scoped, timeboxed no-PO exception for a small pilot. Attachments included. Rafael and FluxOps are asking for a quick decision so they can start next week.

Key details:
- Vendor: FluxOps (startup, US)
- Requested path: invoice-only for pilot <= $10k over 90 days
- Documents: vendor form + W9 + integration scope
- Recommended guardrails: Net 14 or prepaid credit, auto-expire after 90 days, cap spend at $10k

Karthik — can Procurement sign off to a one-off exception with those controls? If you need additional mitigations (e.g., escrowed credit or finance PO tracker), say so and we’ll coordinate. We need a reply to the vendor by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Integration trial — procurement exception request (FluxOps)

Marissa / Rafael — Procurement approves a conditional no-PO onboarding for FluxOps with the following explicit conditions: 
1) Cap at $10k total for pilot; any projected spend beyond that requires a standard PO and SOW.
2) Exception term: 90 days from the first invoice date; Procurement will automatically close the exception in our tracker unless an internal request to convert is sent.
3) Payment cadence: Net 14. If Finance requests prepayment, Rafael should request that from the buyer and document the reason.
4) Security/legal must confirm the integration scope (security contact on the vendor form) before we enable access to any non-prod data.
5) Recordkeeping: Rafael to add the signed vendor form and W9 to the procurement ticket (PROC-2152) and mark the exception record.

I have added the exception to the procurement tracker and linked the HubSpot record (see related_links). Rafael — you can reply to Aisha and confirm. Procurement will provide a short exception memo upon request.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Procurement & Vendor Ops
